title: Securities Dealing Policy
date_approved: Reviewed October 2025; authorised by the Board of Australian Foundation Investment Company Limited
date_next_review: At least every three years, or earlier in response to significant regulatory developments

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel, comprising the Non-Executive Directors of the Company and the Senior Executives (including the Managing Director) as determined by the Board from time to time. All of the section 2 prohibitions, the prohibited periods and the notification regime apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors of the Company, a sub-set of KMP. Distinguished for the notification protocol (prior notice to the Chairman or MD and either the CFO or Company Secretary) and exempt from the section 2.6 hedging ban, which is directed at Senior Executives' performance-based remuneration.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Senior Executives of the Company including the Managing Director, as determined by the Board. Subject to the section 2.6 hedging prohibition over unvested performance-based securities, breach of which will normally result in termination of employment; adherence to the policy is a term of their employment with Australian Investment Company Services Limited.

tiers.name: Closely Connected Persons and Entities
tiers.description: Family members whose financial affairs are controlled by the KMP, and companies, trusts and entities controlled by the KMP. The policy applies to private dealings by these persons in the Company's securities. KMP must also use all reasonable endeavours to ensure a third party through whom they have a reportable interest complies with the policy as if it were a KMP.

definitions.hedging_definition: using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities they may receive as part of their performance-based remuneration (hedging)

windows.end_anchor: the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its interim financial results (inclusive)
the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its final financial results (inclusive)

windows.start_anchor: commencement of the pricing period for any capital management event

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose other periods when employees are prohibited from dealing in the Company's securities because inside information may exist (section 4.2). No approver is named and the policy does not state whether such periods are confidential.

rules.detail: The policy contains no definition of dealing and no derivatives provision. Options, futures and OTC contracts over the Company's securities held outright by a KMP are not named, so the only constraints on a derivative over vested unrestricted holdings are the general prohibitions in section 2 and the prohibited periods.

Use of any financial product to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities received as performance-based remuneration is prohibited for Senior Executives, with termination of employment as the normal consequence.
rules.evidence: Senior Executives are prohibited from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities they may receive as part of their performance-based remuneration (hedging).

rules.detail: Express hedging ban confined to unvested performance-based remuneration securities of Senior Executives. Breach normally results in termination of employment; no clearance or exceptional circumstances route is offered for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: Breaches of the Company's policy in this regard will normally result in the termination of the Senior Executive's employment.

rules.detail: The section 2.6 ban is limited to unvested performance-based securities. Hedging of vested, unrestricted holdings is not addressed; the exclusions in section 3 refer to release of securities from a holding lock or holding term but the policy imposes no restriction on dealing with them once released.
Section 2.6 binds only Senior Executives, and Non-Executive Directors do not receive performance-based remuneration securities, so no hedging prohibition is expressed for them.

Monetisation is not named as such, but any structure that raises cash by giving a lender security over the Company's securities is caught by the blanket ban on using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans. A monetisation that involves no security interest over the shares is not addressed.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling the Company's securities by KMP, with no definition, carve-out or clearance route. The exceptional circumstances relief in section 5 extends only to a sale during a prohibited period.
rules.evidence: KMP must not engage in short-selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no definition of dealing that could sweep it in.

Contracts for difference are not named. A short CFD would engage the section 2.4 short selling ban and any actively traded position would conflict with the section 2.3 requirement that dealings be for investment rather than trading purposes.

Absolute ban on using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements, with no vesting distinction and no approval or exemption route. KMP must additionally use best endeavours to avoid being put in conflict with the policy by margin or other loans over other securities.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans. KMP must also use their best endeavours to ensure they are not put in a position of conflict with this policy by virtue of having margin or other loans over other securities.

rules.detail: Any grant of security over the Company's securities to support a loan is prohibited. The wording covers margin lending arrangements 'or other loans', so a pledge, mortgage or charge in favour of a bank is caught regardless of the loan type or the vesting state of the shares. A charge unconnected with a loan is not addressed.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: Blanket prohibition extending beyond margin lending to any other loan secured on the Company's securities, binding on all KMP and their Closely Connected Persons and Entities. There is no tier, security-state or approval carve-out, and the section 5 exceptional circumstances relief covers only a sale during a prohibited period, not the grant of security.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: KMP must not deal for short-term purposes; dealings must be for investment and not trading, with the intention to hold for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling. No fixed period is specified and no carve-outs are listed.
rules.evidence: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities for short-term purposes. Dealings in the Company's securities must be undertaken for investment purposes and not for trading, that is, the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.

clearance.approver: Prior notice to the Chairman (or in his absence the MD) and either the Chief Financial Officer or the Company Secretary; the Chairman gives notice to the Audit Committee Chairman or the MD and either the CFO or the Company Secretary. For exceptional circumstances clearance during a prohibited period, written approval by the Chairman (or in his absence the MD). No KMP may receive notice of, or approve, their own transaction.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, for any relevant announcement to the ASX
clearance.evidence: The Chairman (or in his absence the MD) and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities. ... The proposed transaction should take place before the next prohibited period as detailed in section 4.

clearance.approver: Prior notice to the Company Secretary, CFO or MD. For exceptional circumstances clearance during a prohibited period, written approval by the MD (or in his absence the Chairman), copied to the Company Secretary who maintains a record of all approvals.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, for any relevant announcement to the ASX
clearance.evidence: The Company Secretary, CFO or MD must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Senior Executives (excluding the MD) in the Company's securities. The proposed transaction should take place before the next prohibited period as detailed in section 4.

short_term.basis: intention at the time of the transaction to hold for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling
short_term.evidence: the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or in his absence the MD) for Directors; MD (or in his absence the Chairman) for Senior Executives
exceptions.evidence: A KMP who is not in possession of inside information may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited by this policy from doing so if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.

A circumstance will be considered exceptional if the KMP in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Company's securities or there is some other overriding legal requirement for them to do so.

exceptions.approver: Board (approval of the plan determining the timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the securityholders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend reinvestment plan, dividend substitution share plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

vesting of the Company's securities as a result of meeting performance hurdles or release of the Company's securities from holding lock or holding term in respect of securities received by Senior Executives as part of performance based remuneration.
transactions conducted between a KMP and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child or other close family member
transfers of Company securities already held by the KMP into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the KMP is a beneficiary
cancellation of the Company's securities as a result of failure to vest or other forfeiture of securities received by Senior Executives as part of performance based remuneration

financing.price_trigger_guidance: KMP must use their best endeavours to ensure they are not put in a position of conflict with this policy by virtue of having margin or other loans over other securities; no loan to value ratio or trigger level is specified.
financing_disclosure: KMP: may be required annually and from time to time to verify in writing that they have complied with this policy, including the section 2.5 ban on using the Company's securities as loan security; verifications retained by the Company Secretary
KMP: the Company Secretary must be advised immediately following any transaction in the Company's securities so that any relevant ASX announcement can be made

exemption_authority: Only a narrow exceptional circumstances discretion: a KMP not in possession of inside information may be given written clearance to sell (but not purchase) securities when otherwise prohibited, where they are in severe financial difficulty or another exceptional circumstance such as a court order applies. Requests go to the Chairman (or MD) for Directors and to the MD (or Chairman) for Senior Executives, must be accompanied by particulars, and no KMP may approve their own transaction. The Company may be required to notify the existence of exceptional circumstances to the ASX. There is no authority to waive the section 2.5 secured financing ban or the section 2.6 hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: the loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every Non-Executive Director and Senior Executive with no approval route and no vesting carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.topic: conflict from loans over other securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must also use their best endeavours to ensure they are not put in a position of conflict with this policy by virtue of having margin or other loans over other securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a facility secured on a different portfolio must not create a position that could force dealings in AFIC securities, so cross-collateralised or portfolio-wide lending is also constrained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The section 3 exclusions list contains no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, in contrast to most ASX trading policies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consistent with the outright ban on pledging, there is no mechanism by which a lender's enforcement sale during a prohibited period would fall outside the policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested executive equity
bespoke_clauses.clause: Senior Executives are prohibited from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities they may receive as part of their performance-based remuneration (hedging). Breaches of the Company's policy in this regard will normally result in the termination of the Senior Executive's employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is narrow, covering only unvested performance equity of Senior Executives, so unfunded put and call legs over vested shares are not themselves prohibited, but the penalty for getting the vesting analysis wrong is dismissal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy defines neither 'deal' nor 'securities' and contains no derivatives, encumbrance or agreement-to-deal limbs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Whether an OTC option over AFIC shares is a 'dealing' requiring prior notice is left open, so the bank should assume the notification requirements apply and seek confirmation from the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman (or in his absence the MD) and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside a prohibited period the regime is prior notification rather than approval, so if the secured financing ban did not apply the option legs would need only notice and immediate post-trade advice to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A KMP ... may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited by this policy from doing so if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only relief available is for an outright sale in a prohibited period; it cannot be used to authorise a pledge, a derivative or a purchase leg such as buying a put.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities during ... the duration of the pricing period for any capital management event.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a listed investment company, capital management events such as placements, buy-backs and share purchase plans create unscheduled blackouts on top of the December and June periods, restricting when any structure could be entered, reset or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP may be required annually and from time to time to verify in writing (including by email) that they have complied with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A KMP with a secured facility over AFIC shares would have to disclose the breach on their annual certification, making the arrangement impossible to maintain quietly.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for AFIC Key Management Personnel. Section 2.5 prohibits KMP from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans, which bars the secured loan leg outright; the ban is drafted to catch any loan, applies to Non-Executive Directors and Senior Executives alike and to their Closely Connected Persons and Entities, and there is no approval, waiver or exceptional circumstances route to relax it. The derivative legs are less constrained: the section 2.6 hedging prohibition reaches only unvested performance-based remuneration securities of Senior Executives, so a put and call over vested unrestricted shares is not expressly prohibited, and outside prohibited periods a KMP need only give prior notice to the Chairman or MD and the CFO or Company Secretary and advise the Company Secretary immediately after the transaction. Any such structure would still have to avoid the December and June prohibited periods and any capital management pricing period, avoid short selling, and be consistent with the requirement that dealings be for investment and not trading purposes. In practice an unfunded collar could be structured but the funding secured on the collared shares cannot, so the bank would need to lend on an unsecured basis or against other collateral entirely.
